questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources of History' refers to.
questions.a: Historical sources are materials that provide information about the past; they include literary and archaeological sources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources of History'.
questions.a: Historians use both literary and archaeological sources to reconstruct the past.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Sources of History'.
questions.a: explain sources of history

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Inscriptions and Edicts' refers to.
questions.a: Inscriptions are writings engraved on stone, metal, or other hard surfaces; edicts are royal orders inscribed for public display.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Inscriptions and Edicts'.
questions.a: Inscriptions are valuable because they are permanent records that cannot be altered.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Inscriptions and Edicts'.
questions.a: explain inscriptions and edicts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Coins as Historical Sources' refers to.
questions.a: Coins provide information about rulers, dates, religion, and trade of their period.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Coins as Historical Sources'.
questions.a: Coins are durable archaeological sources that reveal economic and political history.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Coins as Historical Sources'.
questions.a: explain coins as historical sources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Manuscripts and Literary Sources' refers to.
questions.a: Manuscripts are handwritten documents; literary sources include books, poems, and records from the past.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Manuscripts and Literary Sources'.
questions.a: Literary sources provide detailed information about society, culture, and events.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Manuscripts and Literary Sources'.
questions.a: explain manuscripts and literary sources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dating Historical Events (BC/BCE, AD/CE)' refers to.
questions.a: Historical dates are counted using BC (Before Christ) / BCE (Before Common Era) and AD (Anno Domini) / CE (Common Era).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dating Historical Events (BC/BCE, AD/CE)'.
questions.a: The year 1 CE follows 1 BCE; there is no year zero in this system.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Dating Historical Events (BC/BCE, AD/CE)'.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Timeline of Major Historical Events' refers to.
questions.a: A timeline arranges historical events in chronological order to show their sequence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Timeline of Major Historical Events'.
questions.a: Timelines help understand the order and duration of historical periods.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Timeline of Major Historical Events'.
questions.a: explain timeline of major historical events

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prehistoric and Historic Periods' refers to.
questions.a: Prehistoric periods have no written records; historic periods have written sources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prehistoric and Historic Periods'.
questions.a: The invention of writing marks the boundary between prehistory and history.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Prehistoric and Historic Periods'.
questions.a: explain prehistoric and historic periods

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Historical Sources' refers to.
questions.a: Historical sources are essential for understanding the past accurately and avoiding misinformation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Historical Sources'.
questions.a: Without sources, history would be based on guesses and legends rather than evidence.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Importance of Historical Sources'.
questions.a: explain importance of historical sources
